name: Abū Manṣūr Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn al-Azhar al-Azharī
summary: Lexicographer of Herat, pupil of al-Mundhirī and teacher of Abū ʿUbayd al-Harawī, author of Tahdhīb al-lugha; his entry is one of the few the print adds without a heading in its index.
bio: Al-Azharī took from al-Mundhirī and transmitted from him a saying of al-Mubarrad on the names of one tree by the place where it grows; Abū ʿUbayd al-Harawī, the author of al-Gharībayn, was his pupil.
His great dictionary, Tahdhīb al-lugha, gathers the lexicon of the Basrans and Kufans with what he heard himself from the Bedouin among whom he was a captive. He died in Herat in 370/980.
uncertain: Ibn al-Anbārī gives no year of death; 370/980 is the date in TDV.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 396–397
Ezherî, Muhammed b. Ahmed, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
